source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Measure adherence to infection-prevention practices, identify performance gaps, and use feedback to guide targeted improvement.","B":"Identify individual staff members for punishment, because disciplinary action is the primary purpose of routine infection-control auditing.","C":"Replace ongoing staff education, because strong audit results eliminate the need for reinforcement of infection-prevention practices.","D":"Produce research data only, because routine unit-level audit findings are not intended to guide local quality-improvement work."}}
source_row.rationale: Regular infection control audits (such as direct observation of hand hygiene compliance or PPE use) are intended to objectively measure adherence to infection prevention practices, identify specific gaps or patterns, and guide targeted improvement efforts and education — a quality improvement tool, not primarily a punitive mechanism.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Core Practices, Performance Monitoring and Feedback: monitor adherence to recommended practices and provide prompt, regular feedback using standardized tools and definitions. Current CDC core-practices page reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Infection Prevention Audit and Feedback Strategies
source_row.stem: A hospital's infection prevention team conducts regular audits of hand hygiene compliance and PPE use on nursing units, and a staff member assumes these audits exist mainly to catch people breaking the rules for disciplinary purposes. The purpose of these audits is instead to:
